title: VPC Security: Security Groups, NACLs & Flow Logs
summary: Stateful and stateless traffic filtering, subnet design and network visibility inside a VPC.
tldr: **Security groups** are stateful, attach to ENIs, and have allow rules only. **NACLs** are stateless, attach to subnets, support **deny** rules and evaluate in rule-number order.
Need to block one bad CIDR range? Only a **NACL deny** can do it; security groups can't deny.
Tier-to-tier access should reference the **source security group** (DB allows 5432 from the app SG), not CIDR ranges.
Put only load balancers in public subnets; app and DB tiers go in private subnets with no route to an internet gateway.

keyFacts.text: Ephemeral port range. A custom NACL must allow outbound (or inbound) traffic to these ports, or return traffic is silently dropped.
NACL rules are processed from the lowest rule number; the first match wins, so a deny must have a lower number than the broad allow.
A customer-managed prefix list groups CIDRs, can be shared with AWS RAM, and is referenced in many security groups; update it once.
VPC Flow Logs record ACCEPT/REJECT with IPs and ports, not payloads. Query REJECT records in CloudWatch Logs Insights to find a blocking SG or NACL.

keywords.cue: block a specific malicious CIDR immediately
keywords.answer: NACL inbound deny rule with a low rule number

keywords.cue: DB reachable only from the app tier
keywords.answer: DB security group references the app security group

keywords.cue: custom NACL added, responses never arrive
partner CIDR list used in many SGs across accounts
keywords.answer: Customer-managed prefix list shared with AWS RAM

keywords.cue: find which traffic is being rejected
keywords.answer: VPC Flow Logs to CloudWatch Logs, query REJECT

keywords.cue: only the load balancer is internet-facing
keywords.answer: ALB in public subnets, app and DB in private subnets
Add a secondary CIDR block and new subnets

traps: Security groups **cannot** contain deny rules; any answer that 'denies a CIDR in the security group' is wrong.
Flow logs show metadata only; they can't inspect packet contents (use Traffic Mirroring or Network Firewall).
Adding NACL inbound rules alone isn't enough because NACLs are stateless.
AWS WAF can't be attached to an internet gateway or VPC; it protects ALB, CloudFront, API Gateway, AppSync and similar.
